svg.aria-label: What spec declares: the module contract. Carriers: Stream and Datagram, with PeekableStream and ResolvedWriter. Addresses: Endpoint and Destination, and the Resolver the base transports use. Transport kinds: base stream and datagram transports create, overlay transports wrap (WrapClientStream and WrapServerStream with the transport metadata); implemented are tcp, udp, tls, ws, httpupgrade, fragment and proxy_protocol. Proxy kinds: StreamProxyModule, DatagramOverStreamProxyModule and DatagramProxyModule (none yet), one module registered once for the kinds it fills, with optional UserManager, MuxCoolConfigurable and ProxyRequestTimingConfigurable. Also the sniffer kind with its SniffResult, the DNS server kinds, the API kind, Metadata, the UDP ASSOCIATE and fallback hand-offs, Config and Info on every kind, and the sentinel errors.
svg.title: What spec declares: the module contract

g.text: Transport kinds: base creates, overlay wraps
Proxy kinds: underlying carrier below, payload above

text.tspan: PeekableStream: Peek, PeekExactly (core implements it) · ResolvedWriter (optional)
an IP and a port, already resolved:
exactly one of a domain or an IP,
plus a port; a domain stays a domain
until the base transport resolves it
Resolver: ResolveDomain(ctx, domain) -> addresses. Every base transport resolves through it.
Optional on any transport: TransportInfoProvider reports the application protocols
it speaks or offers (ALPN, checked across a stack) and NeedsNoServerSide.
A protocol that fills several kinds is one module, registered once (StreamAndDatagramOverStreamProxyModule).
Optional on a proxy module: UserManager · MuxCoolConfigurable · ProxyRequestTimingConfigurable ·
(optional, SOCKS5 only): binds the second socket
Info() ModuleInfo{Name, Description}: constant, never from a setting
The ...Module value is its own settings, decoded straight from the config file;
its New... methods build the running parts once, per role.
Not in spec: Router, TrafficHandler, Inbound and Outbound live in core/component.
ErrInvalidUser · ErrUserExists · ErrNoSuchUser · ErrAPI... (one per refusal)
Callers test them with errors.Is; modules never invent parallel ones.
